RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The accused Lieu Vung who was arrested on
behalf of the Public Safety Bureau on 4.4.32 was again
before the Court on 12.4.32 when the following decision
was given:-

"No proof that she committed any crime, she
may be released after obtaining security."

Case B/53776 Sheet No. 3.

Proceedin Mr T. S. Li for the Police.
The Judge asked that the Court be cleared of outsiders.
Accused:- I know the Zong Ming's writing. This letter is not in his handwriting. I do not know the Kyi Loo.
The Judge handed to Mr Li dispatches received from Nanking Military Authorities and also letter written by the Kyi Loo which had been handed to the accused and was opened by her.
Accused after the statement of the Zong Ming was handed to her, said she did not know what it meant. There was another female named Lee Su Ng who lived with her but she did not know whether she was Lee's sister or relation. This Lee Su Ng returned to Chekiang some time ago. I knew her through the introduction of a person named Man.
Judge to accused:- He has already committed suicide and it is for your protection that he wants you to be sent to Nanking, as he suspects other communists may do harm to you. So you might as well tell the truth as to what friends he had and where they are living.
Accused:- Of his friends who visited him I only knew one who came but I do not know his name. I know none of the other friends nor could I understand their language. I do not know where they live. I have not joined any Communist party. Chu Hong was a doctor as he attended to me once, and that is how I knew him. After he left for Nanking, none of his friends came to the place. All I knew was that he was trying to start a sock factory but as he could not get any capital, he went to Nanking to see some friend of his and try to get a job. I do not want to go to Nanking as I have no friends there. I have relations in Shanghai and wish to continue my study here.
Mr Lee:- I have seen the dispatch from Nanking and I see no proof against the accused that she is a Communist nor do they show that she has committed any offense outside of this. They say it is for her own safety that they want her to be sent

over but it seems really that she is being more harmed than being
protected, besides she does not want to go there as she has no friends
or relations there and it is better for her that she stay here. That
is therefore that since no reliable evidence has been produced
against her, but she may be released on the condition prosecutors
provide that when a person is to be handed over to outside authorities
clear written evidence of guilt / must be produced first and then
the person can be handed over. It seems that the action of the Nanking
Military Authorities are not in accordance with law.
The procurator expressed the same opinion as before and added
that there were grave doubts as to the authenticity of the letter
produced.
Judge to Liu Yeu, rep of Nanking Military Authorities. No proof
of complicity has been brought against her and the only reason for wanting
her to go to Nanking is for her own protection and to get the
names and addresses of the other people. But even if she is handed
over, it will be impossible to get the names and addresses of the other
people as they must have moved to new addresses and she would not be
able to know where they are now. The court will send an official
dispatch to Nanking by post explaining the reason of her not being handed
over.
Liu Yeu:- I ask for her to be detained pending my report to
Nanking. Detain her in order that she may give the names and addresses
of the other people mentioned in the dispatch.

INTELLIGENCE REPORT

2. Assistance to Chinese Authorities - one Communist suspect arrested

Acting on the authority of a warrant issued by the Shanghai
Special District Court at the instance of the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau, the Municipal Police at 4.15 p.m. April 4, raided a
Chinese dwelling at No.247 Yoch Ling Li (岳陽新里), Kuling Road,
and arrested a girl student named Lieu Vung-Wo (劉文華), who
is wanted by the Chinese Authorities on a charge of propagating
communism. No communist literature was found on the premises.
The accused will appear before Court on April 5, when an
application for her extradition will be made by the Chinese
Authorities.
